Notes: Jews from Kozhan-Gorodok came as artisans and merchants after railway construction (1884-1886) but initially lacked residence rights; presence of individuals documented
First synagogue (Old Shul) opened 1895; early settlers named (Lichtstein, Ditalowitski, Treybuch) after railway station built c.1880; approximate town Jewish share not given
1897 census: 293 Jews among 3185 inhabitants; Jewish prayer house existed
Luninets became a permitted Jewish settlement in 1900; synagogues (Horodoker and Ashkenazi) built 1905; rabbi Alter Yehuda Zoliar led community for four decades
Russian Wikipedia gives '2232 (8072) Jews - 22.3% of residents' for 1931; figure ambiguous so Population left blank
27 June 1941 bombing killed 207 people many Jewish; German occupation 10 July 1941; 10 Aug 1941 1312 Jewish men aged 18-60 shot in Mogula ravine (event count)

Ghetto established March 1942 holding approx 3000 people from Luninets and nearby villages (includes non-residents); 20 Jan 1942 1816 Jews remained; 4 Sep 1942 remaining 2932 ghetto inmates killed (death toll)
Approx 4300 Jews killed in Luninets ghetto March-September 1942 (death toll; district-wide nearly all Jews killed; Kozhan-Gorodok ~1000; Lakhva >2000)
Red Army liberated town summer 1944 emptied of Jews; about 25-30 survivors regrouped in postwar Poland then emigrated
